newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil limiting import financing - Cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil limiting import financing - Cenbank.

text.p: Brazil will introduce Wednesday new rules to limit the attractiveness of short-term import financing, Gustavo Franco, the Central Bank's International Affairs Director, said.
Franco told reporters most importers with financing of less than 360 days will have to take out foreign exchange contracts on the day they retrieve their goods from customs.
Those who fail to pay on the due date will be fined for every day's delay, he said.
"This equalizes the treatment of imports and exports," Franco said. "I'm convinced this is nothing protectionist as it only affects the capital account."

Long-term financing of more than 360 days, imports by state-owned petroleum company Petrobras and imports worth less than $10,000 are exempt from the new rules, he said. All imports involving up to 180-day financing are legally obliged to take out foreign exchange contracts the day goods are picked up. Imports financed from 180-360 days must have foreign exchange contracts taken out 180 days before payment date.
Franco said that for a long time there had been similar restrictions on export financing but no conditions attached to financing of imports.
This was not equal treatment and ended up creating an imbalance, Franco said.
"Many imports were simply happening because of the financing that went with them...The competitivity of national products was being distorted by this asymetry," he said.
The measure would have an affect on the trade balance but "it would not be significant," Franco said.
"Eliminating this incentive will affect imports," he said, adding that restrictions on the capital account side of trade was "common" in other countries.
Franco said about 25 percent of imports were paid for in cash, 10 percent were paid for with financing of more than 360 days and the rest fell in between.
